title: Critical Abelian Higgs Vortices: Existence, Minima and Flux Cylinders

items.title: Critical Abelian Higgs fields, winding and divisor data
items.statement:
Let $e>0$ and $\xi>0$ be real parameters, set $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, identify the oriented Euclidean plane $\mathbb R^2$ with $\mathbb C$ using coordinates $(x_1,x_2)$, and use the Hodge star convention $*dx_1=dx_2$, $*dx_2=-dx_1$. A field pair is a smooth real one-form $A=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2$ on the trivial complex line over $\mathbb R^2$ and a smooth function $q:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb C$. Its unit-charge covariant derivative is $D_Aq=dq-iAq$, its curvature is $F_A=dA=B\,dx_1\wedge dx_2$ with $B=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, and its transverse energy is
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B^2}{2e^2}+|D_{A,1}q|^2+|D_{A,2}q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2.$$
The pair has finite energy when this nonnegative Lebesgue integral is finite. An admissible boundary sector consists of an integer $n$, a radius $R_0$, and smooth functions $\rho>0$ and real $2\pi$-periodic $\phi$ on $r>R_0$ such that $q(r,\theta)=\rho(r,\theta)e^{i(n\theta+\phi(r,\theta))}$ and $\rho\to\sqrt\xi$, $\phi\to0$ uniformly as $r\to\infty$; $n$ is its winding. A gauge transformation is $(q,A)\mapsto(e^{i\chi}q,A+d\chi)$ for a smooth real-valued function $\chi$ on $\mathbb R^2$.

For $n\ge0$, the positive critical first-order equations are $(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$; for $n\le0$ the negative equations are $(D_{A,1}-iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=-e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$. The adjective critical refers to the displayed energy normalization and these square-saturating equations. For a positive-winding solution, its divisor is an effective finite divisor $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$, where the $z_j\in\mathbb C$ are distinct, the multiplicities $m_j$ are positive integers, $q$ vanishes exactly at the $z_j$, and near each $z_j$ it has the local form $q(z)=(z-z_j)^{m_j}g_j(z)$ with $g_j$ smooth and nonzero there. The degree is $N=\sum_jm_j$; the empty divisor has degree zero. Negative winding uses the conjugate field and reversed orientation, with $N=|n|$.

On the complement of the divisor, define $h=\log(|q|^2/\xi)$. The associated scalar Taubes datum is a real function smooth away from the divisor such that $h-2m_j\log|z-z_j|$ extends smoothly across every $z_j$, $h\to0$ at infinity, and, as a distribution,
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=4\pi\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\delta_{z_j},\qquad \langle\delta_z,\psi\rangle=\psi(z)\quad(\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)).$$
When the limit exists, the magnetic flux is $\Phi(A)=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|<R}B(x)\,dx_1dx_2$. These are mathematical configuration and normalization conventions; they make no assertion that a physical model describes nature.

items.title: Taubes disk barriers and monotone Dirichlet iteration
items.statement:
Let $\kappa>0$ and let $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$ be a finite effective divisor in $\mathbb C$, where the centers $z_j$ are distinct and $m_j\in\mathbb N$; write $N=\sum_jm_j$. For any $a>0$ with $a\ge4N/\kappa$, the function
$$u_-(z)=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\log\frac{|z-z_j|^2}{|z-z_j|^2+a}$$
is a global distributional subsolution of $\Delta u+\kappa(1-e^u)=4\pi\sum_jm_j\delta_{z_j}$. For every $R>\max_j|z_j|$ (with the empty maximum interpreted as $0$), let $D_R=\{|z|<R\}$ and define
$$u_{s,R}(z)=\sum_jm_j\log\frac{R^2|z-z_j|^2}{|R^2-\overline z_jz|^2},\qquad \psi_R(z)=\frac{\kappa}{4}(R^2-|z|^2),\qquad A_R=e^{u_{s,R}}.$$
Then $u_{s,R}$ is the zero-boundary Dirichlet Green sum with $\Delta u_{s,R}=4\pi\sum_jm_j\delta_{z_j}$; $u_{s,R}+\psi_R$ is a supersolution and $u_-\le u_{s,R}+\psi_R$ on $D_R$. Write $H^1_0(D_R;\mathbb R)$ for the closure of $C_c^\infty(D_R;\mathbb R)$ in the real Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(D_R;\mathbb R)$. For any constant $L_R\ge\kappa\max_{\overline D_R}(A_Re^{\psi_R})$, the positive zero-Dirichlet resolver $(-\Delta+L_R)^{-1}$ on $H^1_0(D_R;\mathbb R)$ defines the monotone iteration
$$v_0=u_--u_{s,R},\qquad v_{k+1}=(-\Delta+L_R)^{-1}\bigl(\kappa+L_Rv_k-\kappa A_Re^{v_k}\bigr).$$
It converges pointwise and in $H^1(D_R)$ to a solution $v_R\in C^{2,\alpha}(\overline D_R)$ for every $0<\alpha<1$, with $v_0\le v_R\le\psi_R$ and zero boundary trace. Thus $u_R=u_{s,R}+v_R$ solves the distributional divisor equation, satisfies $u_-\le u_R\le0$, and has $u_R-2\sum_jm_j\log|z-z_j|$ smooth at the centers. For the fixed singular function $s(z)=2\sum_jm_j\log|z-z_j|$, every compact $K\subset\mathbb C$ and every $p>2$ admit constants independent of sufficiently large $R$ such that $u_R-s$ is uniformly bounded in $W^{2,p}(K)$. For each $0<\alpha<1$, choosing $p>2/(1-\alpha)$ also gives a uniform $C^{2,\alpha}(K)$ bound. These are the local compactness estimates for disk exhaustion.

For exhaustion, subtract fixed u_minus, not R-dependent u_sing: on each compact disk its regular difference has bounded Laplacian and bounded boundary values, so local bounds survive R->infinity. items.title: Planar critical vortices for arbitrary finite divisors
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$, $\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and an effective finite divisor $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$ on $\mathbb C$ with distinct centers and positive integer multiplicities; let $N=\sum_jm_j$. There is a unique real scalar function $h$, smooth on $\mathbb C\setminus\{z_j\}$, such that $h-2m_j\log|z-z_j|$ extends smoothly across each center, $h\to0$ as $|z|\to\infty$, and
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=4\pi\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\delta_{z_j}$$
in distributions, where $\langle\delta_z,\psi\rangle=\psi(z)$ for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$. For $N>0$, $h<0$ off the divisor; for the empty divisor, $h=0$. With $P(z)=\prod_j(z-z_j)^{m_j}$, $s=2\log|P|$, and the orientation $*dx_1=dx_2$, $*dx_2=-dx_1$, the fields
$$q(z)=\sqrt\xi\,e^{(h(z)-s(z))/2}P(z),\qquad A=-\tfrac12 *d(h-s)$$
extend smoothly across the centers and solve $(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$, where $D_A=d-iA$ and $B\,dx_1\wedge dx_2=dA$. They have finite energy
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B^2}{2e^2}+|D_{A,1}q|^2+|D_{A,2}q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2$$
and flux $\int_{\mathbb R^2}B\,dx_1dx_2=2\pi N$. For every $0<\alpha<\sqrt\kappa$ and every multi-index $\beta$, $|\partial^\beta h(z)|=O(e^{-\alpha|z|})$ as $|z|\to\infty$; the curvature $B$ and covariant gradient $D_Aq$ have the same exponential decay. On the exterior of a disk, the local gauge $e^{-i\arg P}$ gives $q_{\mathrm{ext}}=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}$ and $A_{\mathrm{ext}}=-\tfrac12 *dh$, so the fields approach the vacuum exponentially in that exterior gauge; the raw global representative $q$ need not have an exponentially small phase correction. Negative winding $-N$ is obtained by complex conjugation and $A\mapsto-A$, with flux $-2\pi N$.

For strict negativity, if w=-h>=0 and Delta w<=kappa w, then w(x)cos(sqrt(kappa)t) is nonnegative superharmonic on a narrow 3D slab; the classical subharmonic strong maximum principle applied to its negative propagates any zero, contradicting logarithmic singularities. Polynomial-phase reconstruction has algebraic phase tails for displaced centres; gauge-invariant h/B/Dq decay exponentially, and a smooth degree-zero exterior gauge cleanup produces canonical field tails.

items.title: Global energy minima for critical Abelian Higgs vortices
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$ and $\xi>0$ and use the critical Abelian-Higgs energy and boundary-sector convention in which $D_A=d-iA$, $B=dA$, $q$ tends in modulus to $\sqrt\xi$, and its exterior phase has winding $n\in\mathbb Z$. For every smooth finite-energy field pair $(A,q)$ in that sector,
$$E(A,q)\ge 2\pi\xi|n|.$$
For $n\ge0$, the exact identity is
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(|(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q|^2+\frac{(B-e^2(\xi-|q|^2))^2}{2e^2}\right)dx_1dx_2+2\pi\xi n;$$
for $n\le0$, replace $D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2}$ by $D_{A,1}-iD_{A,2}$ and $B-e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$ by $B+e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$, with topological term $-2\pi\xi n$. The boundary-current term in the disk identity vanishes along a radius sequence derived from the finite-energy hypotheses. The fields reconstructed for any fixed divisor by the arbitrary-divisor plane theorem attain equality, are absolute transverse energy minima in their winding sector, have zero first variation under smooth compactly supported variations, and have nonnegative second variation in those directions. This does not assert uniqueness of minimizing fields across distinct divisors of the same degree.

items.title: Fixed-flux cylinders and uniform end-collar energy
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$, $\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and $n\in\mathbb Z$. For transverse fields on the oriented Euclidean plane, let $A_\perp=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2$ be a smooth real one-form, let $q:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb C$ be smooth, set $D_iq=(\partial_i-iA_i)q$ and $B_{12}=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, and define
$$E_\perp(A_\perp,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B_{12}^2}{2e^2}+|D_1q|^2+|D_2q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2.$$
For $L>0$, write $\Omega_L=\mathbb R^2\times[0,L]$ with coordinates $(x_1,x_2,z)$, let $\mathcal A=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2+A_3dz$ be a smooth real connection one-form, let $q:\Omega_L\to\mathbb C$ be smooth up to the ends, set $F=d\mathcal A$, $D_\mu q=(\partial_\mu-iA_\mu)q$, and define the full static energy
$$\mathcal E_L(\mathcal A,q)=\int_0^L\!\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left[\frac{B_{12}^2+F_{31}^2+F_{32}^2}{2e^2}+|D_1q|^2+|D_2q|^2+|D_3q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right]dx_1dx_2dz,$$
where $B_{12}=F_{12}$. Call such a pair admissible of winding $n$ if its energy is finite, every transverse slice has finite $E_\perp$, and there are $R_0>0$ and smooth $\rho>0$ and real $2\pi$-periodic $\phi$ on $\{|x|>R_0\}\times[0,L]$ such that $q=\rho e^{i(n\theta+\phi)}$, with $\rho\to\sqrt\xi$ and $\phi\to0$ uniformly in $z$ and $\theta$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Require that each slice has flux $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{D_R}B_{12}\,dx_1dx_2=2\pi n$, and require the angular one-form condition
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{0\le z\le L}\left|\int_{\partial D_R}(A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2-n\,d\theta)\right|=0$$
and zero radial magnetic-flux leakage, meaning that the integral of $F$ over the side $\partial D_R\times[0,L]$ tends to zero as $R\to\infty$. The infimum below is over admissible pairs with fixed smooth finite-energy end traces $p_0=(A^0,q^0)$ and $p_1=(A^1,q^1)$ in winding $n$. If their exterior phase is $n\theta+\phi_j$, first apply the globally smooth degree-zero gauge cleanup proved below and prescribe the resulting representatives as the end values. The common canonical exterior gauge means $q^j=\rho_j e^{in\theta}$ and $A^j-n\,d\theta\in L^2$ outside a disk, with the angular one-form limit above.

For any two such fixed end traces, the cleaned differences $q^1-q^0$ and $A^1-A^0$ lie in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$. Choose any finite collection of distinct points $z_j\in\mathbb C$ with positive integer multiplicities $m_j$ summing to $|n|$ (the empty collection for $n=0$), and let $p_*=(A^*,q^*)$ be its planar minimizing field pair in canonical exterior gauge. Set $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$. There are a fixed collar width $\ell>0$ and finite constants $C_0,C_1$, depending on the end traces, $p_*$, and the chosen smooth collar profile but not on $L$, such that for every $L\ge2\ell$,
$$T_nL\le\inf\mathcal E_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1.$$
Consequently the difference $\inf\mathcal E_L-T_nL$ remains bounded as $L\to\infty$. If both fixed end traces are the same planar minimizing pair, its constant extension in $z$ attains the exact minimum $T_nL$. This is a mathematical fixed-flux boundary variational statement and does not assert a point-source self-energy or a quantum Wilson-loop result.

The gauge transformations used to put an end trace in canonical exterior gauge have the form $(q,A)\mapsto(e^{i\chi}q,A+d\chi)$ for a smooth real-valued function $\chi$ on the whole plane; the function is globally defined by extending a radial cutoff times the single-valued periodic phase correction.

items.title: A double vortex and a separate third vortex
items.statement:
Let $e,\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and let $z_0\ne z_1$ be any two points of $\mathbb C$. For the positive-winding divisor $D=2[z_0]+[z_1]$, whose degree is $3$, the unique scalar solution satisfies
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=8\pi\delta_{z_0}+4\pi\delta_{z_1},\qquad h-4\log|z-z_0|\text{ extends smoothly at }z_0,\qquad h-2\log|z-z_1|\text{ extends smoothly at }z_1,\qquad h\to0\text{ at infinity},$$
with $h<0$ off $\{z_0,z_1\}$. For $P(z)=(z-z_0)^2(z-z_1)$ and $s=2\log|P|$, the reconstructed fields $q=\sqrt\xi e^{(h-s)/2}P$ and $A=-\tfrac12*d(h-s)$ are smooth, have flux $6\pi$, and attain transverse energy $6\pi\xi$. The solution is specified by this unique nonlinear elliptic problem; no elementary closed-form profile is asserted.

Separately, for each $n\in\mathbb Z$ and each effective divisor of degree $|n|$, the corresponding planar minimizer has signed flux $2\pi n$ and transverse energy $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$. For fixed smooth end traces in winding $n$ and the same canonical exterior gauge, its cylinder infimum satisfies
$$T_nL\le\inf\mathcal E_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1\quad(L\ge2\ell),$$
for a fixed collar width $\ell>0$ and finite constants $C_0,C_1$ independent of $L$; matching minimizing end traces give the exact value $T_nL$. This is the fixed-flux variational estimate for the stated cylinder class.
